cohort: The study participants were urban Bangladeshi mothers who had given birth.
finding: The study identified significant socioeconomic and demographic determinants, including wealth, education, media exposure, maternal age, working status, and religion, affecting cesarean section rates among urban Bangladeshi mothers.
mod_finding: Higher wealth, educational attainment, media exposure, and maternal age (20-34 years) were positively correlated with the likelihood of cesarean section delivery, while working status and specific divisions showed inverse associations.
cross-section timing: Data from the Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey (BDHS) 2022-2025 dataset.
